data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The apparent reliability gain of the non-expert panel is often a baseline-rate artifact: on highly skewed outcome distributions, a checklist with high implicit base-rate prior produces high accuracy by tracking the majority class, not by discriminating signal.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Evaluation uses balanced accuracy or area under ROC curve, not raw accuracy; panel's apparent gain disappears under discrimination metrics.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Outcome distribution is not skewed; panel's gain persists on balanced datasets.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Checklist items are shown to have criterion validity independent of base rate (panel discriminates minority cases).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Checklists encode surface cues correlated with the majority outcome.
